summary: Hamilton County, IL, Illinois Division of Forestry tower about 8 miles north of McLeansboro; a woman lookout in 1953-54; demolition bids in 1975; removed.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a metal cab on top
facts.status_note: Removed; no source describes what remains at the site or whether it is open to the public.

events.note: Florence Musgrave of Aden received her appointment as lookout in September 1953; she was the first woman in the Division's history to serve as a lookout from one of its fire towers (per 1954 report)
Invitation to bid on demolition of the lookout published in the Southern Illinoisan, August 11, 1975
Three-acre former tower site offered for sale by sealed bid; bids opened March 25, 1980; minimum $4,900

notes_for_editor: No build date found in any source read; the story leaves it out. The 1961 survey says the station is about 3.5 miles west of Aden, while the 1980 sale notice says the former site is one mile west of Aden on Route 242. The FFLA point (38.24088, -88.51986) was not reconciled with either description, so the coordinates may need a human check. The 1961 survey height (about 110 ft to the top of the cabin) is entered as 33.5 m; it is to the cabin top, not the cab floor. Agency comes from the page's county heading. The 1975 and 1980 items are auction and demolition notices, not confirmations of removal dates, so no removal year is given. The Frakes article says three Illinois towers remain, then names a fourth standing tower (Forest Glenn, Georgetown); the story attributes only the three-count to Frakes and says the article does not list Aden among the towers still standing. The 1961 record is headed National Geodetic Survey but says it was described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey; the story uses that wording.
